entries.text: cloud Networking BGP uses Autonomous System numbers in path information to describe the sequence of autonomous systems through which reachability information has passed.

entries.title: OSPF Link-State Routing
entries.text: cloud Networking OSPF is a link-state interior gateway protocol in which routers build a topology database from link-state advertisements and calculate shortest paths.

entries.title: OSPF Areas
entries.text: cloud Networking OSPF can divide an autonomous system into areas to reduce the amount of routing information that must be distributed everywhere.

entries.title: NTP Clock Synchronization
entries.text: cloud Networking NTP exchanges timestamp information so networked systems can estimate clock offset and delay relative to time sources.

entries.title: Traditional NAT Address Translation
entries.text: cloud Networking Traditional NAT rewrites IP address information as packets cross between address realms and can maintain mappings between internal and external address tuples.

entries.title: VXLAN VNI Scale
entries.text: cloud Networking VXLAN uses a 24-bit VXLAN Network Identifier, allowing far more logical segments than a 12-bit VLAN identifier can encode.

entries.title: SSH Transport Security
entries.text: cloud Networking The SSH transport protocol provides server authentication, confidentiality, and integrity protection for the SSH connection.

entries.title: TLS 1.3 Handshake Keys
entries.text: cloud Networking TLS 1.3 derives traffic keys during the handshake and then protects application records with authenticated encryption.

entries.title: HTTP Cache Validation
entries.text: cloud Networking HTTP caches can validate stored responses with the origin server when freshness information no longer permits direct reuse.

entries.title: Mount Namespaces
entries.text: cloud Linux A Linux mount namespace isolates mount points so processes in different namespaces can have different views of those resources.

entries.title: PID Namespaces
entries.text: cloud Linux A Linux pid namespace isolates process ID number spaces so processes in different namespaces can have different views of those resources.

entries.title: Network Namespaces
entries.text: cloud Linux A Linux network namespace isolates network devices, protocol stacks, routing tables, and related networking state so processes in different namespaces can have different views of those resources.

entries.title: IPC Namespaces
entries.text: cloud Linux A Linux ipc namespace isolates System V IPC objects and POSIX message queues so processes in different namespaces can have different views of those resources.

entries.title: UTS Namespaces
entries.text: cloud Linux A Linux uts namespace isolates hostname and NIS domain name so processes in different namespaces can have different views of those resources.

entries.title: User Namespaces
entries.text: cloud Linux A Linux user namespace isolates user and group ID mappings so processes in different namespaces can have different views of those resources.

entries.title: Cgroup Namespaces
entries.text: cloud Linux A Linux cgroup namespace isolates the cgroup root visible to a process so processes in different namespaces can have different views of those resources.

entries.title: cgroup v2 CPU Controller
entries.text: cloud Linux The cgroup v2 CPU controller distributes processor time among cgroups and can enforce CPU bandwidth limits through controller settings.

entries.title: cgroup v2 Memory Controller
entries.text: cloud Linux The cgroup v2 memory controller accounts for and can constrain memory used by processes in a cgroup.

entries.title: cgroup v2 I/O Controller
entries.text: cloud Linux The cgroup v2 I/O controller can distribute and limit access to block-device I/O among cgroups.

entries.title: cgroup v2 PID Controller
entries.text: cloud Linux The cgroup v2 pids controller can limit the number of processes that may exist in a cgroup.

entries.title: Bash Standard Output Redirection
entries.text: cloud Linux In Bash, > redirects standard output to a file and truncates the target before writing unless shell options change that behavior.

entries.title: Bash Append Redirection
entries.text: cloud Linux In Bash, >> redirects standard output to a file and appends rather than replacing existing file content.

entries.title: Bash Standard Error Redirection
entries.text: cloud Linux In Bash, file descriptor 2 represents standard error and can be redirected independently from standard output.

entries.title: Bash AND and OR Lists
entries.text: cloud Linux Bash && executes the next command only if the previous command succeeds, while || executes the next command only if the previous command fails.

entries.title: Bash Command Substitution
entries.text: cloud Linux Bash command substitution executes a command and replaces the substitution with its standard output after shell-defined newline processing.

entries.title: Bash Quoting
entries.text: cloud Linux Bash quoting mechanisms control which characters retain literal meaning and which expansions the shell performs.

entries.title: /proc Process Information
entries.text: cloud Linux Linux exposes process and kernel information through the proc filesystem, including per-process directories named by process ID.

entries.title: sysfs Device and Kernel Objects
entries.text: cloud Linux sysfs exports a filesystem view of kernel objects, attributes, and relationships so user space can inspect and configure supported kernel state.

entries.title: Hard Links
entries.text: cloud Linux A hard link is another directory entry referring to the same underlying file object, so linked names share the same file contents.

entries.title: Symbolic Links
entries.text: cloud Linux A symbolic link stores a pathname that the filesystem resolves when the link is followed.

entries.title: File Ownership
entries.text: cloud Linux Unix-like files record owner and group identity used together with permission bits and other access-control mechanisms.

entries.title: Active Directory Domain Controllers
entries.text: cloud Windows & Identity Domain controllers host Active Directory Domain Services data and provide authentication and directory services for the domain.

entries.title: Group Policy Processing Scope
entries.text: cloud Windows & Identity Group Policy processing combines applicable local, site, domain, and organizational-unit policies according to Windows Group Policy processing rules.

entries.title: LDAP Bind Operation
entries.text: cloud Windows & Identity LDAP Bind establishes authentication information for a protocol session before other operations are performed with that authorization state.

entries.title: LDAP Search Operation
entries.text: cloud Windows & Identity LDAP Search requests entries from a directory using a base object, scope, filter, and requested attributes.

entries.title: Conditional Access Policies
entries.text: cloud Windows & Identity Microsoft Entra Conditional Access evaluates identity-driven signals and policy conditions to decide whether to grant access, block access, or require controls such as multifactor authentication.

entries.title: Microsoft Intune Device Management
entries.text: cloud Windows & Identity Microsoft Intune is a cloud-based endpoint management service for managing users, devices, applications, and organizational access policies.

entries.title: BitLocker Full-Volume Encryption
entries.text: cloud Windows & Identity BitLocker provides volume encryption for Windows to help protect data against offline access when a device is lost, stolen, or decommissioned.

entries.title: SMB File Sharing
entries.text: cloud Windows & Identity Server Message Block is a Windows file-sharing protocol used for access to files, printers, and other network resources.

entries.title: Kubernetes Pod
entries.text: cloud Cloud A Pod is the smallest deployable compute object in Kubernetes and can contain one or more containers that share defined resources and lifecycle.

entries.title: Kubernetes Pod Restart Policy
entries.text: cloud Cloud A Pod specification defines a restartPolicy that applies to app containers in the Pod; supported values are Always, OnFailure, and Never.

entries.title: Kubernetes Deployment
entries.text: cloud Cloud A Deployment declaratively manages ReplicaSets and Pods and supports rollout and rollback behavior for stateless application updates.

entries.title: Kubernetes ReplicaSet
entries.text: cloud Cloud A ReplicaSet maintains a specified number of matching Pod replicas and is commonly managed indirectly by a Deployment.

entries.title: Kubernetes RollingUpdate Strategy
entries.text: cloud Cloud A Deployment using RollingUpdate gradually scales down the old ReplicaSet and scales up the new ReplicaSet.

entries.title: Kubernetes maxSurge
entries.text: cloud Cloud Deployment maxSurge controls how many Pods may be scheduled above the desired replica count during a rolling update.

entries.title: Kubernetes maxUnavailable
entries.text: cloud Cloud Deployment maxUnavailable controls how many Pods may be unavailable relative to the desired replica count during a rolling update.

entries.title: Kubernetes StatefulSet
entries.text: cloud Cloud A StatefulSet manages Pods that need stable identity, ordered behavior, or persistent storage associations.

entries.title: Kubernetes DaemonSet
entries.text: cloud Cloud A DaemonSet ensures that eligible nodes run a copy of a Pod and is commonly used for node-level agents.

entries.title: Kubernetes Job
entries.text: cloud Cloud A Kubernetes Job creates one or more Pods and tracks them until a specified amount of work completes successfully.

entries.title: Kubernetes CronJob
entries.text: cloud Cloud A CronJob creates Jobs on a repeating schedule described by a cron-style schedule.

entries.title: Kubernetes ConfigMap
entries.text: cloud Cloud A ConfigMap stores non-confidential configuration data in key-value form for consumption by Pods and other workloads.

entries.title: Kubernetes Secret
entries.text: cloud Cloud A Secret stores a small amount of sensitive data such as a password, token, or key, but Kubernetes warns that Secrets are not encrypted in etcd by default unless encryption at rest is configured.

entries.title: Kubernetes Readiness Probe
entries.text: cloud Cloud A readiness probe determines whether a container is ready to receive traffic; failing readiness removes the Pod from matching Service endpoints.

entries.title: Kubernetes Liveness Probe
entries.text: cloud Cloud A liveness probe helps the kubelet decide when a container should be restarted because it is not healthy.

entries.title: Kubernetes Startup Probe
entries.text: cloud Cloud A startup probe delays liveness and readiness checks until an application has successfully started.

entries.title: Kubernetes QoS Guaranteed
entries.text: cloud Cloud A Pod can receive the Guaranteed QoS class when each container has CPU and memory requests equal to its corresponding limits under the documented QoS rules.

entries.title: Kubernetes QoS Burstable
entries.text: cloud Cloud A Pod is classified as Burstable when it does not meet Guaranteed criteria but at least one container has a CPU or memory request or limit.

entries.title: Kubernetes PersistentVolume
entries.text: cloud Cloud A PersistentVolume is a cluster storage resource whose lifecycle is independent of any individual Pod using it.

entries.title: Kubernetes PersistentVolumeClaim
entries.text: cloud Cloud A PersistentVolumeClaim is a user request for storage that can bind to a compatible PersistentVolume.

entries.title: Kubernetes StorageClass
entries.text: cloud Cloud A StorageClass describes classes of storage and parameters used by dynamic provisioning.

entries.title: Kubernetes Taints
entries.text: cloud Cloud A node taint repels Pods that do not have a matching toleration, subject to the taint effect.

entries.title: Kubernetes Tolerations
entries.text: cloud Cloud A Pod toleration allows scheduling behavior with nodes that carry matching taints, but does not itself force the Pod onto those nodes.

entries.title: Kubernetes PodDisruptionBudget
entries.text: cloud Cloud A PodDisruptionBudget limits how many Pods of a replicated application can be voluntarily disrupted at the same time according to its availability constraints.

entries.title: Kubernetes HorizontalPodAutoscaler
entries.text: cloud Cloud A HorizontalPodAutoscaler adjusts the replica count of a scalable workload based on configured metrics and target values.

entries.title: Kubernetes HPA Replica Formula
entries.text: cloud Cloud For a single metric, the HPA algorithm calculates a desired replica count from the current replicas multiplied by the ratio of current metric value to desired metric value, with additional documented tolerance and readin

entries.title: Kubernetes Service ClusterIP
entries.text: cloud Cloud ClusterIP exposes a Service on an internal cluster IP and is the default Service type.

entries.title: Kubernetes Service NodePort
entries.text: cloud Cloud NodePort exposes a Service on a static port on each node in addition to creating the Service cluster IP.

entries.title: Kubernetes Service LoadBalancer
entries.text: cloud Cloud LoadBalancer requests an external load balancer from supporting infrastructure while retaining the Service abstraction.

entries.title: Kubernetes Service DNS Name
entries.text: cloud Cloud Cluster DNS creates DNS names for Services so workloads can discover Services without hard-coding Pod IP addresses.

entries.title: Kubernetes Node Affinity Required Rules
entries.text: cloud Cloud requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution node affinity rules must be satisfied for a Pod to be scheduled onto a node.

entries.title: Kubernetes Node Affinity Preferred Rules
entries.text: cloud Cloud preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution node affinity rules influence scheduler scoring but are not mandatory placement constraints.

entries.title: Kubernetes CPU Requests
entries.text: cloud Cloud Kubernetes uses CPU requests when scheduling Pods and treats CPU as a compressible resource.

entries.title: Kubernetes Memory Requests
entries.text: cloud Cloud Kubernetes uses memory requests for scheduling and can enforce memory limits through the container runtime and kernel mechanisms.

entries.title: AWS Route Table Longest Prefix Match
entries.text: cloud Cloud Amazon VPC route selection uses the most specific matching route when multiple routes match a destination.

entries.title: Azure Load Balancer
entries.text: cloud Cloud Azure Load Balancer distributes Layer-4 TCP and UDP traffic across backend resources using configured frontend, rule, probe, and backend-pool settings.

entries.title: Terraform Configuration Language
entries.text: cloud Cloud Terraform configuration describes infrastructure declaratively using blocks, arguments, expressions, and references in the Terraform language.

entries.title: Prometheus Time Series
entries.text: cloud Observability Prometheus stores data as labeled time series identified by metric name and a set of key-value labels.

entries.title: PromQL Instant Vector
entries.text: cloud Observability PromQL instant-vector selectors return the latest sample for each matching time series at a single evaluation time.

entries.title: Observability Traces
entries.text: cloud Observability Distributed traces represent the path of a request through a system as spans that can be correlated across services.

entries.title: Observability Metrics
entries.text: cloud Observability Metrics are numeric measurements collected over time and are useful for aggregating system behavior such as rates, counts, utilization, and latency distributions.

entries.title: Observability Logs
entries.text: cloud Observability Logs are timestamped event records that provide contextual information about discrete system events.

entries.title: Backup Restore Testing
entries.text: cloud Recovery Recovery capability is not demonstrated merely by creating backups; restore procedures and backup integrity need to be tested as part of contingency readiness.

entries.title: DNS Zone Delegation
entries.text: cloud Networking DNS delegation places authority for a child portion of the namespace at designated name servers and links parent and child zones with referral information.

entries.title: DNS Authoritative Server
entries.text: cloud Networking An authoritative DNS server answers from authoritative zone data for names within the zones it serves rather than recursively resolving every query.

entries.title: DNS Resolver
entries.text: cloud Networking A DNS resolver is the component that accepts application queries and obtains answers from local information, cache, or other name servers.

entries.title: ICMP Destination Unreachable
entries.text: cloud Networking ICMP Destination Unreachable messages report defined conditions in which a datagram cannot be delivered to its destination or upper-layer endpoint.

entries.title: ICMP Time Exceeded
entries.text: cloud Networking ICMP Time Exceeded messages report when an IP datagram is discarded because its lifetime expired in transit or fragment reassembly time expired.

entries.title: TCP Checksum
entries.text: cloud Networking TCP includes a checksum that covers the TCP header and data together with an IP pseudo-header used to detect corruption and misdelivery.

entries.title: TCP Retransmission Timer
entries.text: cloud Networking TCP uses a retransmission timeout derived from measured round-trip timing so unacknowledged data can be retransmitted after loss.

entries.title: IPv6 Router Solicitation
entries.text: cloud Networking IPv6 hosts send Router Solicitation messages to prompt routers to generate Router Advertisements sooner than the next periodic advertisement.

entries.title: IPv6 Neighbor Solicitation
entries.text: cloud Networking IPv6 Neighbor Solicitation messages support address resolution, reachability confirmation, and duplicate-address detection behavior.

entries.title: IPv6 Neighbor Advertisement
entries.text: cloud Networking IPv6 Neighbor Advertisement messages advertise a node’s link-layer reachability or respond to Neighbor Solicitations.

entries.title: DHCP Client BOUND State
entries.text: cloud Networking After successful DHCP configuration, a client enters a bound state in which it can use the assigned network parameters until renewal or lease expiration behavior applies.

entries.title: DHCP Rebinding
entries.text: cloud Networking If normal renewal does not succeed, a DHCP client can enter rebinding and broadcast requests to available DHCP servers before the lease expires.

entries.title: NTP Stratum
entries.text: cloud Networking NTP uses stratum values to describe a server’s distance in the synchronization hierarchy from a reference clock.

entries.title: systemd Service Units
entries.text: cloud Linux systemd service units describe processes that systemd starts, stops, supervises, and tracks as services.

entries.title: systemd Socket Activation
entries.text: cloud Linux systemd socket units can listen on sockets and activate associated services when traffic arrives.

entries.title: systemd Timer Units
entries.text: cloud Linux systemd timer units activate other units according to monotonic or calendar-based timers.

entries.title: systemd Target Units
entries.text: cloud Linux systemd target units group and synchronize other units and are commonly used to represent system states or boot milestones.

entries.title: systemd Ordering Dependencies
entries.text: cloud Linux systemd distinguishes ordering relationships such as Before and After from requirement relationships such as Wants and Requires.

entries.title: cgroup v2 Hierarchy
entries.text: cloud Linux cgroup v2 uses a single unified hierarchy in which controllers are enabled for child cgroups through documented subtree-control rules.

entries.title: Linux Bridge Forwarding Database
entries.text: cloud Linux A Linux bridge maintains a forwarding database that maps learned MAC addresses to bridge ports for Layer-2 forwarding.

entries.title: Kubernetes Service Selector
entries.text: cloud Cloud A Kubernetes Service selector identifies Pods whose endpoints should back the Service when selector-based endpoint management is used.

entries.title: Kubernetes Headless Service
entries.text: cloud Cloud A headless Service sets clusterIP to None so DNS can return endpoint information without allocating a virtual cluster IP for proxy-based load balancing.

entries.title: Kubernetes StatefulSet Stable Identity
entries.text: cloud Cloud StatefulSet Pods receive stable ordinal identities that persist logically across replacement.

entries.title: Kubernetes StatefulSet volumeClaimTemplates
entries.text: cloud Cloud StatefulSet volumeClaimTemplates create PersistentVolumeClaims for Pods so each replica can have persistent storage associated with its stable identity.

entries.title: Kubernetes PodDisruptionBudget minAvailable
entries.text: cloud Cloud A PodDisruptionBudget can specify minAvailable to state how many selected Pods must remain available during voluntary disruptions.

entries.title: Kubernetes PodDisruptionBudget maxUnavailable
entries.text: cloud Cloud A PodDisruptionBudget can specify maxUnavailable to limit how many selected Pods may be unavailable during voluntary disruptions.

entries.title: Lab: Translate a Virtual Address
entries.text: advanced Memory Virtual-to-physical translation uses page-table indexes plus a page offset; translation caches such as TLBs can avoid repeated page-table walks.

entries.title: Lab: Schedule Tasks Round Robin
entries.text: advanced Memory POSIX SCHED_RR gives equal-priority runnable threads bounded execution intervals and places a thread at the tail of its priority list after its round-robin interval expires.

entries.title: Lab: Train a One-Bit Branch Predictor
entries.text: advanced Memory A one-bit branch predictor can predict the next outcome using only the most recently observed outcome for the same branch; this is an educational microarchitecture model, not a claim about a specific current CPU.

entries.title: Lab: Explore the Roofline Bound
entries.text: advanced Memory The Roofline model relates attainable floating-point performance to arithmetic intensity, peak compute throughput, and memory bandwidth; the basic ceiling is the minimum of peak compute and bandwidth multiplied by arithm

entries.title: Lab: Visualize a Parallel Reduction
entries.text: advanced Memory A parallel reduction combines many input values into progressively fewer partial results until one aggregate remains; this lab visualizes a common tree-shaped reduction implementation.

entries.title: Lab: Measure a Bell Pair
entries.text: advanced Quantum A Bell-state circuit can produce strongly correlated computational-basis outcomes when both qubits are measured in the same basis.

entries.title: Lab: Watch Warp Divergence
entries.text: advanced GPU Computing Divergent control flow within a warp can force the hardware to execute different paths separately for different subsets of threads.

entries.title: Lab: Map Threads to CUDA Blocks
entries.text: advanced GPU Computing CUDA thread and block indices map kernel instances to positions in a grid so each thread can select a portion of the problem.

entries.title: Lab: Match MPI Messages
entries.text: advanced HPC MPI receives can match messages by communicator, source, and tag according to the MPI point-to-point matching rules.

entries.title: Lab: Elect a Raft Leader
entries.text: advanced Distributed Systems A Raft candidate becomes leader when it receives votes from a majority of servers in the cluster for the current term.

entries.title: Lab: Compare Page and TLB Behavior
entries.text: advanced Memory A TLB hit can provide a cached translation, while a TLB miss can require a page-table walk before memory access proceeds.

entries.title: Troubleshooting: GPU Kernel Has Low Occupancy
entries.text: advanced GPU Computing Low occupancy can result when per-block threads, registers, or shared-memory requirements prevent many warps from residing concurrently on an SM.

entries.title: Troubleshooting: MPI Program Hangs
entries.text: advanced HPC MPI programs can hang when processes wait indefinitely for matching communications or collective participation that never occurs.

entries.title: Troubleshooting: NUMA Access Is Slow
entries.text: advanced Memory Remote NUMA memory access can have different latency and bandwidth characteristics from local-node access, so poor placement can reduce performance.

entries.title: Instruction Set Architecture
entries.text: advanced Architecture An instruction set architecture defines programmer-visible machine instructions, registers, data types, addressing rules, and architectural behavior that software targets.

entries.title: Instruction Decode
entries.text: advanced Architecture Instruction decode interprets an encoded machine instruction so the processor can determine the operation and operands required by the architecture.

entries.title: General-Purpose Registers
entries.text: advanced Architecture General-purpose registers provide low-latency architectural storage locations that instructions can use for operands and results.

entries.title: Program Counter
entries.text: advanced Architecture The program counter or instruction pointer identifies the instruction address used to control sequential execution, subject to branches, calls, exceptions, and other control transfers.

entries.title: Processor Pipeline
entries.text: advanced Architecture A processor pipeline overlaps stages of multiple instructions so different instructions can be fetched, decoded, executed, and retired concurrently.

entries.title: Pipeline Data Hazard
entries.text: advanced Architecture A data hazard occurs when an instruction depends on a result that an earlier instruction has not yet made available at the required pipeline point.

entries.title: Pipeline Control Hazard
entries.text: advanced Architecture A control hazard occurs when the processor does not yet know which instruction stream should execute after a branch or other control transfer.

entries.title: Branch Prediction
entries.text: advanced Architecture Branch prediction speculates on control-flow direction or target so instruction fetching can continue before the branch result is fully resolved.

entries.title: Speculative Execution
entries.text: advanced Architecture Speculative execution performs work before all controlling conditions are known and commits architectural effects only when the speculation is validated.

entries.title: SIMD Instructions
entries.text: advanced Architecture SIMD instructions apply one operation to multiple packed data elements, enabling data-level parallelism.

entries.title: Cache Line
entries.text: advanced Architecture CPU caches transfer and track memory in fixed-size blocks commonly called cache lines rather than fetching arbitrary individual bytes independently.

entries.title: Cache Associativity
entries.text: advanced Architecture Set-associative caches divide storage into sets and allow each memory block to occupy one of multiple ways within the indexed set.

entries.title: Cache Conflict Miss
entries.text: advanced Architecture A conflict miss occurs when multiple active memory blocks compete for the limited ways of the same cache set.

entries.title: Cache Capacity Miss
entries.text: advanced Architecture A capacity miss occurs when the active working set exceeds the effective capacity of a cache even without pathological mapping conflicts.

entries.title: Write-Back Cache
entries.text: advanced Architecture A write-back cache can update cached data first and defer writing modified lines to lower memory until eviction or another coherence event requires it.

entries.title: Translation Lookaside Buffer
entries.text: advanced Memory A TLB caches recently used virtual-to-physical address translations to reduce page-table walks.

entries.title: Page Table Walk
entries.text: advanced Memory When a translation is not available in translation caches, hardware or software walks hierarchical page tables to resolve the virtual address mapping.

entries.title: Virtual Address
entries.text: advanced Memory A virtual address is the address generated by a program before the memory-management unit translates it into a physical address.

entries.title: Physical Address
entries.text: advanced Memory A physical address identifies a location in physical memory after address translation.

entries.title: Page Offset
entries.text: advanced Memory The low-order bits of a virtual address select the byte offset within a page and are preserved through ordinary page translation.

entries.title: NUMA Node
entries.text: advanced Memory NUMA systems organize processors and memory into nodes where memory access cost can depend on which processor accesses which memory.

entries.title: Page Cache
entries.text: advanced Memory Linux uses the page cache to retain file-backed data in memory so later reads can often avoid storage access.

entries.title: Anonymous Memory
entries.text: advanced Memory Anonymous memory represents process memory such as heap and stack mappings that is not directly backed by a named file.

entries.title: Memory Reclaim
entries.text: advanced Memory Linux memory reclaim frees or repurposes reclaimable pages when the system needs memory for other uses.

entries.title: Linux EEVDF Scheduler
entries.text: advanced Operating Systems Linux EEVDF uses virtual runtime, lag, eligibility, and virtual deadlines to choose which runnable task should execute next.

entries.title: Runnable Task
entries.text: advanced Operating Systems A runnable task is eligible for CPU scheduling because it is not blocked waiting for an external event.

entries.title: Virtual Runtime
entries.text: advanced Operating Systems Linux fair-scheduling designs track virtual runtime so CPU service can be compared among runnable tasks with different histories and weights.

entries.title: Context Switch
entries.text: advanced Operating Systems A context switch changes the processor from executing one task context to another and therefore requires saving and restoring task execution state.

entries.title: Privilege Level
entries.text: advanced Operating Systems Processor privilege mechanisms restrict sensitive operations so operating systems can protect kernel state from unprivileged software.

entries.title: Trap and Exception
entries.text: advanced Operating Systems A trap or exception transfers control to privileged software at a defined handler so exceptional conditions and protected operations can be processed.

entries.title: OpenMP Parallel Region
entries.text: advanced Parallel Computing An OpenMP parallel construct creates a team of threads that execute a structured block in parallel according to the OpenMP execution model.

entries.title: OpenMP Worksharing Loop
entries.text: advanced Parallel Computing OpenMP loop worksharing distributes iterations of an associated loop among threads in the current team.

entries.title: OpenMP Barrier
entries.text: advanced Parallel Computing An OpenMP barrier synchronizes threads so each participating thread waits until all participating threads reach the barrier.

entries.title: OpenMP Critical Region
entries.text: advanced Parallel Computing An OpenMP critical construct restricts execution of the associated region so only one thread at a time executes a critical region with the same name.

entries.title: OpenMP Atomic Operation
entries.text: advanced Parallel Computing OpenMP atomic constructs provide constrained atomic access to a storage location for supported update, read, write, compare, or capture forms.

entries.title: OpenMP Task
entries.text: advanced Parallel Computing An OpenMP task represents a unit of work that may be executed by a thread in the team according to task scheduling rules.

entries.title: OpenMP Shared Variable
entries.text: advanced Parallel Computing An OpenMP shared variable refers to one storage location visible to participating threads in the data environment.

entries.title: OpenMP Private Variable
entries.text: advanced Parallel Computing An OpenMP private variable gives each participating task or thread a separate storage instance according to the directive semantics.

entries.title: MPI Communicator
entries.text: advanced HPC An MPI communicator defines a group of processes together with a communication context used to isolate message traffic.

entries.title: MPI Rank
entries.text: advanced HPC Each process in an MPI communicator has an integer rank that identifies it within that communicator.

entries.title: MPI Point-to-Point Send
entries.text: advanced HPC MPI point-to-point communication sends messages between a source rank and destination rank within a communicator.

entries.title: MPI Message Tag
entries.text: advanced HPC MPI point-to-point messages can carry integer tags that receivers use together with source and communicator information for message matching.

entries.title: MPI Blocking Receive
entries.text: advanced HPC A blocking MPI receive does not return until the receive buffer can be safely used by the caller according to the MPI completion semantics.

entries.title: MPI Barrier
entries.text: advanced HPC MPI_Barrier blocks participating processes until all processes in the communicator have entered the barrier.

entries.title: MPI Gather
entries.text: advanced HPC MPI_Gather collects equal-size contributions from all processes and places the combined result at the root process.

entries.title: MPI Scatter
entries.text: advanced HPC MPI_Scatter distributes distinct chunks of a root process buffer to participating processes.

entries.title: MPI Collective Communication
entries.text: advanced HPC MPI collective operations involve all processes in a communicator and provide standardized patterns such as broadcast, gather, scatter, reduce, and barrier.

entries.title: Slurm Job
entries.text: advanced HPC A Slurm job is an allocation of resources requested by a user for executing work on a managed cluster.

entries.title: Slurm Partition
entries.text: advanced HPC A Slurm partition groups nodes into a scheduling set and can carry limits and policies that affect jobs submitted to it.

entries.title: Slurm sbatch
entries.text: advanced HPC sbatch submits a batch script to Slurm and returns after the job has been accepted for scheduling.

entries.title: Slurm srun
entries.text: advanced HPC srun launches parallel or serial tasks within a Slurm allocation or can request an allocation for an interactive step.

entries.title: Slurm Job Step
entries.text: advanced HPC A Slurm job step is a set of tasks launched within a job allocation, commonly through srun.

entries.title: CUDA Thread
entries.text: advanced GPU Computing A CUDA thread executes one instance of a kernel and has built-in indices used to determine which data it should process.

entries.title: CUDA Thread Block
entries.text: advanced GPU Computing A CUDA thread block is a group of threads that can cooperate through shared memory and block-level synchronization.

entries.title: CUDA Grid
entries.text: advanced GPU Computing A CUDA kernel launch organizes thread blocks into a grid.

entries.title: CUDA Warp
entries.text: advanced GPU Computing CUDA hardware schedules threads in groups called warps; on current NVIDIA CUDA architectures a warp contains 32 threads.

entries.title: CUDA Warp Divergence
entries.text: advanced GPU Computing Threads in a warp that take different control-flow paths can require the warp to execute those paths separately, reducing effective parallel efficiency.

entries.title: CUDA Registers
entries.text: advanced GPU Computing CUDA registers are per-thread storage allocated from each streaming multiprocessor register file.

entries.title: CUDA Constant Memory
entries.text: advanced GPU Computing CUDA constant memory is a read-only memory space visible to device code and backed by a cache optimized for certain access patterns.

entries.title: CUDA Coalesced Global Loads
entries.text: advanced GPU Computing CUDA combines a warp’s global-memory accesses into the number of memory transactions needed to cover the requested address segments; efficient coalescing minimizes unnecessary transactions.

entries.title: CUDA Occupancy
entries.text: advanced GPU Computing CUDA occupancy is the ratio of active warps on a streaming multiprocessor to the maximum active warps supported by that multiprocessor.

entries.title: CUDA Register Pressure
entries.text: advanced GPU Computing High per-thread register use can reduce the number of resident blocks or warps that fit on a streaming multiprocessor.

entries.title: CUDA Shared-Memory Pressure
entries.text: advanced GPU Computing High per-block shared-memory use can reduce the number of thread blocks that can reside concurrently on a streaming multiprocessor.

entries.title: CUDA __syncthreads
entries.text: advanced GPU Computing __syncthreads() is a block-level barrier that waits until participating threads in the block reach the barrier and makes prior shared/global memory accesses visible according to CUDA synchronization semantics.

entries.title: Lamport Happens-Before Relation
entries.text: advanced Distributed Systems Lamport defines a happens-before relation that orders events when one event causally precedes another through process order or message transmission.

entries.title: Lamport Logical Clock
entries.text: advanced Distributed Systems A Lamport logical clock assigns scalar timestamps that preserve happens-before ordering: if event a happens before event b, then the clock value of a is smaller than the clock value of b.

entries.title: Concurrent Distributed Events
entries.text: advanced Distributed Systems Two distributed events are concurrent under Lamport’s relation when neither event happens before the other.

entries.title: Raft Commit Majority
entries.text: advanced Distributed Systems Raft commits entries from the current term when they are stored on a majority of servers under the protocol’s commitment rules.

entries.title: Raft Log Matching Property
entries.text: advanced Distributed Systems Raft’s log-matching property ensures that if two logs contain an entry with the same index and term, the logs are identical through that index.

entries.title: Qubit State Vector
entries.text: advanced Quantum A pure qubit state can be represented by two complex amplitudes whose squared magnitudes sum to one.

entries.title: Computational Basis Measurement
entries.text: advanced Quantum Measuring a qubit in the computational basis produces 0 or 1 with probabilities given by the squared magnitudes of the corresponding amplitudes.

entries.title: Pauli Z Gate
entries.text: advanced Quantum The Pauli Z gate leaves |0⟩ unchanged and multiplies |1⟩ by -1, changing relative phase.

entries.title: Quantum Tensor Product
entries.text: advanced Quantum The state space of multiple qubits is formed with tensor products, so two qubits are represented in a four-dimensional complex vector space.

entries.title: Bell State
entries.text: advanced Quantum A Bell state is a maximally entangled two-qubit state with measurement correlations that cannot be represented as independent single-qubit pure states.

entries.title: Quantum Circuit
entries.text: advanced Quantum A quantum circuit represents an ordered sequence of quantum operations and measurements applied to qubit registers.

entries.title: Quantum Measurement Shots
entries.text: advanced Quantum On quantum hardware and shot-based simulators, repeated circuit executions produce a distribution of classical measurement outcomes.

entries.title: Relative Phase
entries.text: advanced Quantum Relative phase between amplitudes can change interference and therefore affect later measurement probabilities.

entries.title: Unitary Quantum Gate
entries.text: advanced Quantum Ideal closed-system quantum gates are represented by unitary operators that preserve state-vector norm.

entries.title: Quantum Entanglement
entries.text: advanced Quantum Entangled states are joint multi-qubit states that cannot be written as a tensor product of individual subsystem states.

entries.title: Quantum Interference
entries.text: advanced Quantum Quantum algorithms can combine amplitudes so some computational paths reinforce while others cancel before measurement.

entries.title: Load-Store Architecture
entries.text: advanced Architecture RISC-V base integer instructions access memory through explicit load and store instructions while arithmetic instructions operate on registers.

entries.title: Aligned Memory Access
entries.text: advanced Architecture Processor architectures define alignment behavior for memory operands; aligned access means the address satisfies the alignment requirement of the access size or instruction.

entries.title: Little-Endian Byte Order
entries.text: advanced Architecture Little-endian systems store the least-significant byte of a multibyte integer at the lowest memory address.

entries.title: Atomic Read-Modify-Write
entries.text: advanced Architecture Atomic read-modify-write instructions perform a memory update as one indivisible operation with architecture-defined ordering semantics.

entries.title: Memory Fence
entries.text: advanced Architecture A memory fence constrains the ordering or visibility of memory operations according to an architecture’s memory model.

entries.title: Cache Hit
entries.text: advanced Architecture A cache hit occurs when the requested memory block is present in the cache level being checked.

entries.title: Cache Miss
entries.text: advanced Architecture A cache miss occurs when the requested memory block is absent from the cache level and must be obtained from another level of the memory hierarchy.

entries.title: Memory Latency
entries.text: advanced Architecture Memory latency is the time between issuing a memory request and receiving the requested data or completion response.

entries.title: Memory Bandwidth
entries.text: advanced Architecture Memory bandwidth describes the rate at which data can be transferred through a memory subsystem over time.

entries.title: Working Set
entries.text: advanced Architecture A working set is the subset of code and data actively used during a phase of execution; performance can improve when the working set fits efficiently within faster levels of the memory hierarchy.

entries.title: Data-Level Parallelism
entries.text: advanced Architecture Data-level parallelism exists when the same operation can be applied independently across multiple data elements, enabling SIMD or vector execution.

entries.title: Thread-Level Parallelism
entries.text: advanced Architecture Thread-level parallelism executes multiple independent or partially independent instruction streams concurrently on cores or hardware thread contexts.

entries.title: Vector Register
entries.text: advanced Architecture Vector or SIMD registers store multiple data elements so one instruction can operate on several elements at once.

entries.title: Branch Misprediction
entries.text: advanced Architecture A branch misprediction occurs when speculative control-flow prediction is wrong and incorrectly fetched or executed work must be discarded before correct execution continues.

entries.title: Pipeline Stall
entries.text: advanced Architecture A pipeline stall delays instruction progress because a required operand, resource, translation, or control decision is not yet available.

entries.title: Micro-operations
entries.text: advanced Architecture Some complex machine instructions are decoded internally into one or more simpler micro-operations that the processor schedules and executes.

entries.title: Retirement
entries.text: advanced Architecture Instruction retirement commits completed instruction results to the architectural state in program order on processors that support precise out-of-order execution.

entries.title: Hardware Multithreading
entries.text: advanced Architecture Hardware multithreading allows one physical core to maintain and schedule more than one architectural thread context.

entries.title: Demand Paging
entries.text: advanced Operating Systems Demand paging brings a virtual page into physical memory when it is needed rather than requiring every mapped page to be resident in advance.

entries.title: Page Fault
entries.text: advanced Memory A page fault occurs when address translation or access permissions require the operating system to handle a virtual-memory event before execution can continue.

entries.title: Dirty Page
entries.text: advanced Memory A dirty page contains modified data that has not yet been synchronized to its backing storage and therefore must be written before the page can be safely discarded when persistence is required.

entries.title: Memory Compaction
entries.text: advanced Memory Linux memory compaction moves movable pages to create larger physically contiguous free regions.

entries.title: OOM Killer
entries.text: advanced Memory Linux can invoke the out-of-memory killer when memory cannot be reclaimed sufficiently to satisfy allocation demands, selecting processes for termination according to kernel policy.

entries.title: NUMA Memory Policy
entries.text: advanced Memory Linux NUMA memory policy lets software influence which NUMA nodes are preferred or allowed for memory allocation.

entries.title: Page Table Hierarchy
entries.text: advanced Memory Linux page tables are hierarchical structures whose levels progressively translate portions of a virtual address toward a physical page mapping.

entries.title: TLB Miss
entries.text: advanced Memory A TLB miss means the required virtual-to-physical translation is not present in the translation cache and another translation mechanism such as a page-table walk is required.

entries.title: Page Walk Cache
entries.text: advanced Memory Some processors cache intermediate page-table information in dedicated page-walk caches to reduce translation overhead.

entries.title: Kernel Privilege
entries.text: advanced Operating Systems Operating systems execute privileged kernel code with access to processor facilities and memory that user-mode code cannot directly access.

entries.title: OpenMP static Schedule
entries.text: advanced Parallel Computing An OpenMP static loop schedule assigns iteration chunks to threads before the loop executes according to the static scheduling rules.

entries.title: OpenMP dynamic Schedule
entries.text: advanced Parallel Computing An OpenMP dynamic loop schedule assigns chunks to threads as threads become available, enabling work redistribution during execution.

entries.title: OpenMP guided Schedule
entries.text: advanced Parallel Computing An OpenMP guided schedule assigns chunks dynamically while generally decreasing chunk sizes as work proceeds until a minimum chunk size is reached.

entries.title: OpenMP nowait Clause
entries.text: advanced Parallel Computing The OpenMP nowait clause removes the implicit barrier from constructs where the specification permits nowait.

entries.title: OpenMP taskwait
entries.text: advanced Parallel Computing OpenMP taskwait suspends the current task until specified child or dependent tasks complete according to taskwait semantics.

entries.title: OpenMP task depend
entries.text: advanced Parallel Computing OpenMP depend clauses express ordering dependencies between sibling tasks based on matching dependence information.

entries.title: OpenMP collapse Clause
entries.text: advanced Parallel Computing The OpenMP collapse clause associates multiple nested loops with a loop directive so their iteration spaces are combined according to specification rules.

entries.title: OpenMP firstprivate
entries.text: advanced Parallel Computing OpenMP firstprivate gives each task or thread a private copy initialized from the original variable’s value before the region executes.

entries.title: OpenMP lastprivate
entries.text: advanced Parallel Computing OpenMP lastprivate can copy the value from the logically last iteration or section back to the original variable according to directive semantics.

entries.title: MPI Allgather
entries.text: advanced HPC MPI_Allgather gathers each process contribution and distributes the complete gathered result to every participating process.

entries.title: MPI Alltoall
entries.text: advanced HPC MPI_Alltoall performs a personalized all-to-all exchange in which each process sends a distinct block to every other process.

entries.title: MPI Reduce_scatter
entries.text: advanced HPC MPI_Reduce_scatter reduces distributed values and scatters portions of the reduced result among participating processes.

entries.title: MPI Scan
entries.text: advanced HPC MPI_Scan performs an inclusive prefix reduction so each process receives the reduction of values from lower ranks through its own rank.

entries.title: MPI Exclusive Scan
entries.text: advanced HPC MPI_Exscan performs an exclusive prefix reduction in which each process receives the reduction of values from lower ranks, excluding its own contribution.

entries.title: MPI Probe
entries.text: advanced HPC MPI_Probe lets a process inspect an incoming matching message status before receiving the message payload.

entries.title: MPI ANY_SOURCE
entries.text: advanced HPC MPI_ANY_SOURCE can be used in a receive to accept a matching message from any source rank in the communicator.

entries.title: MPI ANY_TAG
entries.text: advanced HPC MPI_ANY_TAG can be used in a receive to accept a matching message with any tag.

entries.title: MPI Derived Datatype
entries.text: advanced HPC MPI derived datatypes describe noncontiguous or structured memory layouts so communication routines can transfer logical data structures without manual packing in many cases.

entries.title: MPI Cartesian Topology
entries.text: advanced HPC MPI supports Cartesian virtual topologies that map ranks into multidimensional grids and provide topology-aware rank-coordinate helpers.

entries.title: CUDA threadIdx
entries.text: advanced GPU Computing CUDA exposes threadIdx so device code can identify a thread’s index within its block.

entries.title: CUDA blockDim
entries.text: advanced GPU Computing CUDA exposes blockDim so device code can determine the dimensions of its thread block.

entries.title: CUDA gridDim
entries.text: advanced GPU Computing CUDA exposes gridDim so device code can determine the dimensions of the launched grid.

entries.title: CUDA Memory Transaction
entries.text: advanced GPU Computing CUDA global-memory requests from threads in a warp are serviced with memory transactions covering the required address segments.

entries.title: CUDA Shared-Memory Bank Conflicts
entries.text: advanced GPU Computing Shared-memory accesses can serialize when multiple threads in a warp contend for the same memory bank under access patterns that create bank conflicts.

entries.title: CUDA Pinned Host Memory
entries.text: advanced GPU Computing Page-locked host memory can improve host-device transfer behavior and is required for some forms of truly asynchronous host-device memory copy.

entries.title: CUDA Asynchronous Copy
entries.text: advanced GPU Computing CUDA supports asynchronous operations that let data movement and computation overlap when hardware capabilities, memory types, and stream dependencies permit it.

entries.title: CUDA Event
entries.text: advanced GPU Computing CUDA events can record points in stream execution and are commonly used for synchronization and elapsed-time measurement on the device timeline.
